seo_description: Free, open-source menu bar app for macOS. Switch any display's resolution and refresh rate, save layouts as profiles, and apply them with a hotkey.
hero_sub: ResolutionHopper lives in your menu bar and lists every mode for every connected display. Save your layout as a profile, then apply it from the menu or with a global hotkey.
features_sub: A small, native menu bar utility for people with external monitors, projectors and capture cards.

features.title: Every mode, grouped clearly
features.desc: Each display gets a submenu of modes grouped by resolution and sorted by refresh rate. HiDPI and stretched modes are labelled, and the current mode is checked.

features.title: Profiles for whole layouts
features.desc: Save the current mode of all displays as a named profile and apply it in one click. Entries for displays that are not connected are skipped and reported in the menu.

features.title: Global hotkeys per profile
features.desc: Record a shortcut for any profile in Settings. Hotkeys use Carbon RegisterEventHotKey, so no permission is needed.

features.title: 15-second Keep or Revert
features.desc: After each switch you get a countdown to keep the change or revert. It runs on a main run loop timer, so it still fires if the screen goes black.

features.title: Automatic rules
features.desc: Apply a profile automatically when a chosen external display connects. Displays are matched by vendor, model and serial number, not display ID.

features.title: Local, with no network calls
features.desc: No analytics and no third-party dependencies, only Apple frameworks. Profiles are stored as JSON on your Mac.

permissions_step: No special permissions are required; if you turn on Launch at login, macOS may list the app under System Settings > General > Login Items.

faq.q: Is ResolutionHopper really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. If you find it useful, there is an optional Support button that opens a Ko-fi page.

None for normal use. It does not request Accessibility or Screen Recording, and hotkeys work without a permission prompt. Only if you enable Launch at login may it appear under Login Items in System Settings.
Profiles are saved as JSON at ~/Library/Application Support/ResolutionHopper/profiles.json. The app makes no network calls, other than opening the Ko-fi page in your browser when you click Support.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
